title: Build your first report
subtitle: A useful result. Clear boundaries. Evidence you can inspect.
courseLabel: Harness in practice · Tutorial 2 of 6 · Plan → Build

sections.title: Build a report you can explain
sections.intro: Turn six synthetic activity entries into an HTML report. Keep the input and tests unchanged.
sections.html:
Open the sample report. Look for 6 entries and 270 minutes, with 180 minutes for Orion and 90 for Lumen.

You will preview the work, approve its scope, run the local build and inspect the result. The practice worker supplies reference code. The local reviewer exercises the review protocol. The tests check the resulting program, and the practice makes no model calls.

For a project that needs more preparation, compare the goal-driven and spec-driven approaches.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to explain the useful result and next decision in their own words.
Keep this offline practice distinct from authorizing real project or model work.

sections.title: Start in an isolated practice folder
sections.intro: Use the terminal and Python environment from course setup.
sections.html:
Complete course setup and keep the extracted folder open in the same terminal, with COURSE_WORK set.

Run the practice setup command below. It creates the sample project in $PRACTICE/project and writes the draft work request to $PRACTICE/task.work.json. Keep this terminal open for the rest of the lesson.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to explain the useful result and next decision in their own words.
Keep this offline practice distinct from authorizing real project or model work.

sections.title: Ask what may change and how it will be checked
sections.intro: Preview the request and check the proposed scope.
sections.html:
Run the plan command below. Look for draft, an empty list of missing questions and a checkpoint_digest.

Confirm that the goal and both test criteria match the exercise. The plan may change only report.py. It protects the CSV, expected reports, tests, participant registry and pytest configuration.

If the preview needs a correction, stop and revise the request through the supported workflow. Generate a fresh preview before you accept its scope.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to explain the useful result and next decision in their own words.
Keep this offline practice distinct from authorizing real project or model work.

sections.title: Agree to the exact request
sections.intro: Accept the exact draft you reviewed. You authorize execution in the next step.
sections.html:
If the preview matches the exercise, replace the placeholder in PREVIEW_CHECKPOINT with the full checkpoint_digest from your preview. Run the command below.

Look for accepted and a new checkpoint. That records your approval of the reviewed scope. You are ready to decide whether to run the build.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to explain the useful result and next decision in their own words.
Keep this offline practice distinct from authorizing real project or model work.

options.text: Agreement to the displayed scope; execution is still separate.
options.feedback: The saved request is accepted. Starting the local command workers is the next decision.

options.text: The report has already been implemented and checked.
options.feedback: Acceptance records intent, not implementation or test evidence.

sections.title: Give the local commands a bounded go
sections.intro: Review the local participant commands and authorize the practice build.
sections.html:
Check the two local commands in $PRACTICE/project/participants.json and the effects in the accepted plan. Run build with --allow-external to authorize those commands for this practice run.

Look for completed after the configured checks pass. If the build fails, read the saved error and journal before choosing what to do next.

For real model work, check your selected route in the participant setup and funding guide.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to explain the useful result and next decision in their own words.
Keep this offline practice distinct from authorizing real project or model work.

sections.title: Separate a completed task from a trustworthy claim
sections.intro: Check the saved task for the change and test results.
sections.html:
Run status below to inspect $PRACTICE/task. Under Planned tasks, look for report.py in Outputs. Under Host checks, look for Passed beside probe:change and probe:final.

The course compatibility results record 77 passing cases per probe in the tested exercise. Use your own task record to see what ran in your environment.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to explain the useful result and next decision in their own words.

sections.title: Take the checked result into your browser
sections.intro: Generate the report from the unchanged six-row CSV.
sections.html:
Run the report command below. It writes $PRACTICE/activity-report.html beside the project. Look for Saved report to … and open that file in your browser.

Check the count, 270 minutes, project totals and date range against the CSV. Choose a new output filename if you run the command again.

sections.title: Leave the work ready to inspect tomorrow
sections.intro: Explain one result, one boundary and the next decision.
sections.html:
This lesson saves your note in this browser when storage is available. Keep the paths to $PRACTICE/task and $PRACTICE/activity-report.html for the next lessons.

Next: Open Come back tomorrow to return to the saved task.
